senses.definition: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of apologize.

quotes.text: The Rector sconced him in the buttery-book, but Webberly “wiped it off, with irreverent and unbeseeming language.” For this, he had to apologise, and go without his commons for three months.
quotes.reference: 1898, Rev. A. Clark, University of Oxford, College Histories: Lincoln, page 73:

quotes.text: At the other extreme, couples who are married with children have heavily disguised tiffs. A man saying in a slightly strained way, 'I'm going to turn the compost', is actually saying, 'And that's all you are, Jean, compost!' Of course, what happens is eventually he apologises, they cry, make love, have another child, get overtired and the tiffing continues.
quotes.reference: 2000 September 30, Guy Browning, “How to... have a tiff”, in The Guardian:

quotes.text: John Mayer has apologised for using a racist epithet in a recent interview with Playboy magazine, after a number of prominent black musicians aired their disapproval.
quotes.reference: 2010 February 11, Rosie Swash, “John Mayer apologises after using N-word in Playboy interview”, in The Guardian:
